passage: Careers With over 19,000 employees, CFISD is one of the largest employers in the Houston area. We have openings for professional, administrative, admin support and clerical, technical and labor, and many more! Select from the many career paths offered at CFISD. The Many Rewards of Working in CFISD CFISD offers a team-oriented workplace that encourages personal and professional growth and success. To help you achieve your goals, we ensure a supportive atmosphere throughout all campuses and departments. Whether it is assisting new educators learn the latest researched-based practices or supporting existing employees reach their goals, our strong belief in training and collaboration makes all the difference in the lives of each member of the CFISD team. Get to Know Us CFISD is leading the way in creating a new vision for public education in Texas. We are dedicated individuals who are passionate about education and helping students achieve their full potential. Our schools and departments are staffed by competent, committed adults who are supported and appreciated, and who understand their first priority is the children they serve. It is through our collaborative efforts amongst a wide range of dynamic employees that sets us apart from other school districts across the state and makes us exceptional. Throughout the year, CFISD continuously seeks high-quality applicants to fill a wide range of positions available at our 92 campuses and many departments. We encourage you to explore the Job Seekers section of the website to learn more information about career opportunities and the benefits of working in CFISD. For questions regarding teacher positions, please call (281) 897-4050. For all other positions within the district, please call (281) 897-4189 or email Human Resources. Professional Growth Opportunities We know that great educators want to continue to learn and grow. At Cy-Fair ISD, the growth opportunities are as diverse as our many schools, facilities and the caring professionals who staff them. We work closely with teachers and support staff to plan and deliver a wide range of exciting and innovative professional growth opportunities, including: - Leadership Development Program & Leadership Development Continuum - Personal Development - Staff Development Destination District CFISD is more than just a school district—it’s a community where students grow, learn, and often return to give back as educators and staff. As a destination district, CFISD takes pride in the many employees who were once students here, inspired by their own experiences to shape the next generation. With a strong culture of support, innovation, and professional growth, CFISD provides opportunities for alumni to build fulfilling careers in the same schools that shaped their futures. Our commitment to excellence, coupled with a deep sense of belonging, makes CFISD a place where careers come full circle, turning former students into the dedicated leaders of today. QUALIFICATIONS: 1. High school diploma or GED equivalent. 2. Three (3) years of administrative assistant experience or three (3) years of experience in human resources. 3. Proficient in the use of personal computer software such as Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Adobe. 4. Ability to quickly learn various Human Resource computer programs. 5. Experience utilizing and maintaining a variety of databases with the ability to export data and reports from a variety of sources. 6. Demonstrated ability to work with a wide range of individuals and complex issues. 7. Demonstrated personal integrity and ability to maintain confidentiality. 8. Ability to perform a variety of tasks and change assignments on short notice, with little or no direction. 9. Ability to multi-task various administrative activities/duties. 10.Strong and effective oral and written communication skills required. 11.Strong attention to detail and organizational skills required. 12.Strong decision-making skills and demonstrated personal integrity required to support the best interest of the district. TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT: 250 days SALARY: $38,008 - CP6 Salary Range (based on experience) as set by the Board of Trustees for the school year 2022-2023 ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: 1. Receive and initiate the workflow process for new hire paraprofessional recommendations. 2. Coordinate contract signings and I-9 meetings for new hires. 3. Setup RIVS interviews for assistant director. 4. Review and rate references for new hires. 5. Process payroll actions such as resignations and transfers. 6. Create and maintain spreadsheets for new hires, staff lists, etc. 7. Track and update educational aide certification for current CP2/IP2 paraprofessionals. 8. Assist employees with questions regarding general district policies. 9. Assist with keeping all HR social media platforms updated. 10.Prepare and run reports as needed. 11.Maintain confidentiality of information. 12.Assist with special projects as needed. 13.Assist with organization of CFISD Career Fair and participate in recruiting efforts. 14.Promote and support departmental goals. 15.Perform other duties as assigned by the director/assistant directors of paraprofessional and support staff. 16.Regular and reliable attendance is an essential job function. WORKING CONDITIONS: Mental Demands/Physical Demands/Environmental Factors: Standard office equipment including personal computer and peripherals. Work with frequent interruptions; maintain emotional control under stress. Prolonged sitting, repetitive hand motions, frequent keyboarding and use of mouse; occasional light lifting and carrying (less than 15 pounds). Payroll The payroll department is responsible for processing all full time, part time, substitute and temporary employee’s pay checks accurately and timely on a semi-monthly basis. Additional duties include the withholding and remittance of mandatory deductions such as Teacher Retirement System contributions, Federal Tax withholding and Medicare deductions. Compensation Plan To ensure a strategic and efficient allocation of resources, the Human Resources department collaborated with the Texas Association of School Boards to establish the foundation for the district’s compensation plan. The updated pay structure is designed to promote pay equity and enhance market competitiveness by aligning job midpoints with current market data. As part of this effort, the plan includes a revised hiring schedule to guide teacher salary placement, as well as a midpoint-based pay structure for non-teaching positions to ensure alignment with prevailing market rates. Compensation plan highlights: - Teachers: Average of 6.2% increase (Starting pay for first-year teachers is $62,000) - 0-2 years of experience - $1,250 increase - 3-4 years of experience - $2,500 increase - 5+ years of experience - $5,000 increase - Non-teaching positions: 2% of midpoint general compensation increase - Bus drivers: Average of 8.6% increase to a starting pay of $24 an hour - Health insurance: An increase of $25 per month for the health insurance premium contribution The district is dedicated to reviewing the comprehensive compensation plan annually and updating it as needed to recruit new employees and remain competitive. Karen Smith, Cy-Fair ISD's chief financial officer, proposed a 2% pay increase for all CFISD staff in a preliminary fiscal year 2022-23 budget presentation at the May 9 board meeting. The board of trustees indicated a desire for a 4% salary increase at the expense of taking a month’s worth of the district’s reserves to foot the bill over a timeframe not to exceed five years. The district is planning for a $1.1 billion budget, 89.6% of which is dedicated to payroll costs. However, with just over $1.06 billion in revenue expected, the current outlook leaves CFISD with a $77 million shortfall. Smith said she anticipates federal pandemic relief funds known as the Elementary and Secondary School Emergency Relief Fund to cover that deficit. Pay increases would also extend to substitute teachers, increasing daily pay from $92 to $110. Pay increases were also included for custodial staff, raising their pay to $12 an hour. Custodial pay was a point of concern among senior board members, who recalled past pay rates of $8 per hour, reflecting systemic minimal increases in pay for custodial staff. Another benefit CFISD staff will see is a decrease in insurance premiums, showing a change in what is typically seen by staff members, officials said. Board President Tom Jackson proposed updating the pay increase to 4% and using a month of the backup funding that is stored to alleviate the deficit that would ensue. Jackson also referred to reinstating keeping full-time substitute teachers on campuses to alleviate teacher burdens for peer absences. Trustee Julie Hinaman recommended taking on a tiered approach in distributing pay raises. This idea was corroborated by Trustee Natalie Blasingame, who said she wants to see more funds applied to paraprofessionals and to support disciplinary efforts. Teacher compensation data from neighboring districts revealed CFISD pays more than most, competing mostly with Spring Branch ISD. While CFISD has higher pay for retained teachers, SBISD had a higher starting salary of $59,000 for FY 2021-22. Staff vacancies sit at 400-450, excluding bus drivers and custodial staff, and the district is aiming to fill these positions. Funding the budget Smith said developing the budget is often a balancing act between local property taxes and state aid. This is reflected when property values increase, as they have this year, leading to less funding. State aid is allotted based on enrollment, average daily attendance, special populations and property wealth. Data from the Harris County Appraisal District showed the upcoming fiscal year will see a 13% increase in taxable property values. The increases do not provide additional funding to the school but to the state, officials said. Based on anticipated revenue for fiscal year 2022-23, the state is contributing about 38% of funding compared to 53% in local property taxes. According to Smith, the state funding formula pays out a flat $6,160 per student without an adjustment for inflation. While that allotment remains the same, according to Smith and Hinaman the cost of educating a CFISD student is $9,356 per student, a $3,196 difference. To review the full presentation, follow this link. The board is expected to approve the 2022-23 budget in June.

HOUSTON — The Houston Independent School District will begin linking teacher compensation to classroom effectiveness starting in the 2026–2027 school year, district leaders announced Tuesday afternoon in a livestreamed update. "At the end of the day, we want to ensure that your children have effective, proficient teachers, educators who nurture them and help them achieve, whether it’s reading, writing, math or preparation for college and career. This pay-for-performance model helps us do that," HISD Superintendent Mike Miles said during the announcement. "Yes, it’s about teachers, but more importantly, it’s about our students and making sure they get the highest quality education possible. And that starts with an effective teacher in every classroom." Under the new pay-for-performance model, teacher salaries will be based on individual effectiveness rather than seniority. The district’s Teacher Excellence System (TES), already in use, will serve as the foundation for evaluations. Miles said more than 10,500 evaluations have already been conducted using TES, which assesses instruction, outcomes, planning, and professionalism. “It’s time for teachers to earn a professional wage, not just a living wage,” Miles said. Approximately 60% of HISD teachers are expected to earn ratings of “Proficient” or higher under the system, the superintendent said. “No organization can value performance and pay based on something else,” Miles said. To ease the transition, teachers’ salaries during the 2025–26 school year will be “held harmless,” meaning no one will earn less than they would have under the traditional pay schedule. Additionally, salaries will not decrease for at least four years, even if a teacher’s evaluation rating drops, HISD Chief of Schools Sandi Massey said. "I worked very hard as a teacher. I had effective scores for my students all 12 years, and yet I got paid the same as the teacher across the hallway who had just started,” Massey said of her time teaching. Starting in 2026, new teachers will earn a base salary of $70,000, while those with three or more years of experience will start at $74,000. The highest earners, teachers rated as Exemplary 1, can make up to $92,000 annually. Educators in New Education System (NES) schools will receive between $3,000 and $9,000 more than their peers at Priority and Underserved Area, or PUA, campuses, depending on their effectiveness rating. Ongoing compensation will be determined using a two-year average TES score. Support programs such as Trailblazers and TES coaching will be in place to help educators adjust to the new system. “Great teachers who are effective deserve great compensation,” Massey said. Jackie Anderson, Houston Federation of Teachers president, released the following statement after HISD's announcement: "We are not happy with a pay-for-performance scheme.
